# logos nogo checkescape through the real compiled archive: an annotated
# heap-escaping function fails at its original allocating statement in Go
# and in .lgo, a single-statement allow silences only its own statement, an
# allocation-free annotated function stays clean, a malformed annotation is
# descriptive, and --json-diagnostics names nogo::checkescape. Helper lives
# at $GOROOT/lib/logos-nogo; behavior only, no source wiring or registry
# count. Fixtures import nothing and use no network.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

mkdir $WORK/bin

# An annotated heap escape fails at the allocating statement in Go. The
# detail names the compiled allocator call, never the "(possible, ...)"
# objdump-failure fallback.
cd goscape
! logos lint ./...
stderr 'main\.go:13:.*\[nogo::checkescape\].*heap:.*runtime\.(newobject|mallocgc)'
! stderr 'possible'
! stderr 'eject'
logos build -o $WORK/bin/goscape$GOEXE .
! stderr .
# std vet has no checkescape.
go vet ./...
! stderr 'nogo::'
cd ..

# --json-diagnostics names the rule at the same line with deny severity.
cd goscape
! logos lint --json-diagnostics ./...
stderr -count=1 '^\{.*\}$'
stderr '"schema_version":"1\.0"'
stderr '"rule_id":"nogo::checkescape"'
stderr '"severity":"deny"'
stderr '"file":"[^"]*main\.go"'
stderr '"span":\{"start_line":13,'
stderr '"provenance":'
stderr '"autofix_candidates":\[\]'
! stderr '^#'
! stderr 'warning:'
cd ..

# An allow silences exactly one statement: the allowed leak passes while
# the next annotated leak still fails.
cd goscapeallowed
! logos lint ./...
stderr 'main\.go:17:.*\[nogo::checkescape\].*heap:.*runtime\.(newobject|mallocgc)'
! stderr 'main\.go:11:'
! stderr 'possible'
stderr -count=1 '\[nogo::checkescape\]'
cd ..

# An annotated but allocation-free function stays clean.
cd gonoscape
logos lint ./...
! stderr .
cd ..

# A malformed annotation (space, not colon) is descriptive, not silent.
cd gobadescape
! logos lint ./...
stderr 'main\.go:5:.*\[nogo::checkescape\].*malformed checkescape annotation'
stderr -count=1 '\[nogo::checkescape\]'
cd ..

# The same heap escape in .lgo maps to the original .lgo line, never the
# ejected temp. A real lowering (a chain lambda) sits above the finding,
# so only exact original-coordinate mapping reports the shifted line.
cd lgoescape
! logos lint ./...
stderr 'main\.lgo:19:.*\[nogo::checkescape\].*heap:.*runtime\.(newobject|mallocgc)'
! stderr 'possible'
! stderr 'eject'
logos build -o $WORK/bin/lgoescape$GOEXE .
! stderr .
cd ..

# --json-diagnostics for .lgo names the original .lgo file at the same line.
cd lgoescape
! logos lint --json-diagnostics ./...
stderr -count=1 '^\{.*\}$'
stderr '"schema_version":"1\.0"'
stderr '"rule_id":"nogo::checkescape"'
stderr '"severity":"deny"'
stderr '"file":"[^"]*main\.lgo"'
stderr '"span":\{"start_line":19,'
stderr '"provenance":'
stderr '"autofix_candidates":\[\]'
! stderr '^#'
! stderr 'eject'
cd ..

# An allow in .lgo silences exactly one statement at original coordinates.
cd lgoescapeallowed
! logos lint ./...
stderr 'main\.lgo:23:.*\[nogo::checkescape\].*heap:.*runtime\.(newobject|mallocgc)'
! stderr 'main\.lgo:17:'
! stderr 'possible'
stderr -count=1 '\[nogo::checkescape\]'
cd ..

# Plain go has no lint command and no --json-diagnostics flag.
cd goscape
! go lint ./...
stderr 'unknown command'
! go build --json-diagnostics ./...
stderr 'flag provided but not defined: -json-diagnostics'
cd ..

-- goscape/go.mod --
module example.com/goscape

go 1.27

-- goscape/main.go --
package main

type Box struct {
	v int
}

// Leaky allocates on the heap and must be diagnosed.
// +checkescape:heap
//
//go:noinline
//go:nosplit
func Leaky() *Box {
	return new(Box)
}

func main() {
	b := Leaky()
	println(b.v)
}

-- goscapeallowed/go.mod --
module example.com/goscapeallowed

go 1.27

-- goscapeallowed/main.go --
package main

type Box struct {
	v int
}

// Leaky is allowed and must stay silent.
// +checkescape:heap
//logos:allow(nogo::checkescape)
func Leaky() *Box {
	return new(Box)
}

// AlsoLeaky is a second violation past the allow and must still fail.
// +checkescape:heap
func AlsoLeaky() *Box {
	return new(Box)
}

func main() {
	a := Leaky()
	b := AlsoLeaky()
	println(a.v, b.v)
}

-- gonoscape/go.mod --
module example.com/gonoscape

go 1.27

-- gonoscape/main.go --
package main

// Pure performs no allocation and must stay silent.
// +checkescape:heap
//
//go:noinline
//go:nosplit
func Pure(a, b int) int {
	return a + b
}

func main() {
	println(Pure(1, 2))
}

-- gobadescape/go.mod --
module example.com/gobadescape

go 1.27

-- gobadescape/main.go --
package main

// Broken carries a malformed annotation (space, not colon).
// +checkescape all
func Broken() int {
	return 1
}

func main() {
	println(Broken())
}

-- lgoescape/go.mod --
module example.com/lgoescape

go 1.27

-- lgoescape/main.lgo --
package main

type Box struct {
	v int
}

// doubled exercises real lowering above the finding: the eject rewrites
// the chain lambda, so only exact mapping reports the shifted line below.
func doubled(xs []int) []int {
	return xs.map(x => 2*x)
}

// Leaky allocates on the heap and must be diagnosed.
// +checkescape:heap
//
//go:noinline
//go:nosplit
func Leaky() *Box {
	return new(Box)
}

func main() {
	ys := doubled([]int{1, 2, 3})
	println(len(ys))
	b := Leaky()
	println(b.v)
}

-- lgoescapeallowed/go.mod --
module example.com/lgoescapeallowed

go 1.27

-- lgoescapeallowed/main.lgo --
package main

type Box struct {
	v int
}

// doubled exercises real lowering above the finding: the eject rewrites
// the chain lambda, so only exact mapping reports the shifted line below.
func doubled(xs []int) []int {
	return xs.map(x => 2*x)
}

// Leaky is allowed and must stay silent.
// +checkescape:heap
//logos:allow(nogo::checkescape)
func Leaky() *Box {
	return new(Box)
}

// AlsoLeaky is a second violation past the allow and must still fail.
// +checkescape:heap
func AlsoLeaky() *Box {
	return new(Box)
}

func main() {
	ys := doubled([]int{1, 2, 3})
	println(len(ys))
	a := Leaky()
	b := AlsoLeaky()
	println(a.v, b.v)
}
